title: Onramp mosaic: compact entry tiles, progressive ribbons, and contextual screenshot scaffolding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and deliver a compact, modular hero/entry experience for the Quickstart landing page that focuses on a mosaic of entry tiles, progressive ribbon explanations, and a scaffold for contextual product screenshots. Goal: reduce cognitive load on first visit, improve completion rate of first-run checklist, and provide developers with clear, copy + visual hooks that map to the three main onboarding flows (API quickstart, SDK samples, Console tour). Deliverables: responsive mosaic components (desktop/tablet/phone), three ribbon copy variants for progressive reveal, screenshot capture spec and automation notes, export-ready assets and dev handoff tokens.

Prototype: InVision hosted flow (link in comments)

decisions: Prefer static pre-rendered screenshots for reproducibility and security (no embedded live sessions)
Use a 3-tile mosaic on desktop; collapse to single-row horizontal carousel with accessible controls on small screens
Progressive ribbon copy limited to three steps; each ribbon exposes a single CTA to reduce friction
Micro-animations limited to hover and focus states; no auto-play or heavy Lottie animations to keep initial page load under 300ms on 3G emulation
tradeoffs: Static screenshots reduce perceived freshness vs live embeds but minimize security and complexity
Opting for sprite icons reduces network requests but increases build step complexity for docs pipeline
Keeping ribbons shallow (3 steps) may omit deeper nuance for advanced users but improves first-time completion
